40.name: Sofle
40.description: 12u columnar stagger with a number row. Open source with many varieties.

40.name: corne (crkbd)
40.description: 12u (or 10u) columnar stagger. Open source with many varieties

60.name: neo60
60.description: Rolling release. Grommet gasket pcb-mounted 60%. Maybe some wireless option. Cheap and fancy.

60.name: QK60
60.description: Acrylic top, aluminum bottom 60. Plate gasket mount. Cheap and fancy.

60.name: Keychron Q4, V4 (Max)
60.description: Q4's the metal one, V4's the plastic one. Has your foam, and silicone blubber bottom in the V4. Supports QMK/VIA. Max model is wireless.

60.name: HHKB Professional Classic
60.description: The big round bump of Topre isn't something you'll find in MX based switches. Simple and reliable, and allergic to modifications. Some people swear by it.

60.name: Tofu60 Redux
60.description: You bought a Wooting60 and now you want to put the PCB in a fancy metal case.

75.name: Realforce RC1
75.description: Topre in a 75% case. Portable like an HHKB, only with a function row and 2U shift key. Has bluetooth!

75.name: Keychron V1/Q1
75.description: Same deal as the rest, the V series is plastic and the Q series is metal. The Max model is wireless. It's a 75 with foam and a knob! What more could you want

75.name: Monsgeek M1
75.description: Similar to Keychron Q1: a gasket mounted 75 with foam and a knob for a competitive price. M1W is wireless and might not support VIA.

75.name: Lemokey X4
75.description: Like a Keychron V1, but cheaper, and without hotswap. Still supports QMK/VIA, still has gamer lights.

75.name: Sat75X
75.description: Gasket mounted 75% with a knob and an OLED, only it's not slop like the others.

75.name: Keychron K2
75.description: Older, condensed 75% layout. Supports bluetooth by default, but the Max model supports QMK/VIA. 'Aluminum frame' means there's a strip of aluminum running around the lip of the plastic case.

TKL.name: Keychron Q3/V3
TKL.description: Q's the metal one, V's the plastic one. Standard Keychron design language in TKL size. Supports QMK/VIA.

TKL.name: Tiger Lite Gaming
TKL.description: Look out, we got an important gamer here! Here's the one with the PCB for you, stop yammering about how you wouldn't be hardstuck in Wood if you had access to rapid trigger or whatever

TKL.name: Leopold FC750RBT
TKL.description: Classic Leopold tank quality, now with bluetooth. Doubleshot PBT keycaps. Buy this if you don't plan on modifying it.

TKL.name: Filco Majestouch
TKL.description: If it ain't broke, don't fix it. Buy this if you don't plan on modifying it. Doubleshot caps (sometimes), costar stabilizers. The standard of TKL.

TKL.name: MK870
TKL.description: Translucent plastic tray mounted TKL with boatload of RGB in the correct orientation. It just works, no stupid glued on wireless module, no battery that catches on fire.

TKL.name: Keychron C1/C1 Pro/C3 Pro
TKL.description: C1's a regular tray mounted plastic TKL, C3 is gasket mounted. It just works. Pro series can be configured with QMK/VIA

TKL.name: Varmilo VA87M
TKL.description: Classic floating key TKL. Buy this if you don't plan on modifying it.

TKL.name: KBD8X MKIII
TKL.description: Lot of metal keyboard for not much money. A lot of colors, WKL options, foam, and a cool lightbar

TKL.name: NCR80
TKL.description: Looks like an old Cherry G80, feels like one too. But it's got a modern PCB!

TKL.name: Realforce R3
TKL.description: Topre in TKL form. R3 is wireless. R3S is lasered on legends. R2 is same case as R3 with dye-sub legends.

TKL.name: Classic-TKL
TKL.description: Plastic gasket mounted TKL with a lightbar and design language of a Realforce R1. They put the USB port in a good place.

TKL.name: Lemokey X1
TKL.description: Plastic tray mount TKL from a Keychron sub-brand. Cheap, simple, supports QMK, has a few gamer lights.
